correctness.rationale: Blockwise symmetric eigenvalue perturbation proves G=spread(U^TDU), L=norm(PDu) with fixed-D and uniform bounded-D error controls. Coordinate rank-one probes give the necessary equal squared normal components and exclude zeros. Explicit orthonormal compression proves balanced sufficiency and coefficient sqrt(2). Known lower-branch uniform CDF is independently derived by a three-coordinate cube-volume calculation, and continuous mapping proves the joint event limit. Symbolic and direct-eigensolver checks were replayed; finite trials are not proof.

originality.rationale: A complete iff condition for samplewise proportionality of two first-order numerical quantities is proved on every rank-one three-coordinate orientation. The source paper provides separate bounds, while classical sample-variance formulas account for the marginalized CDF and are explicitly excluded from novelty. Known graph-specific finite-amplitude covariance does not imply or cover the iff classification; exact equivalence elsewhere remains a residual literature risk.
residual_risks: The if-and-only-if property may appear as a small-dimensional lemma in older spectral-compression or diagonal-perturbation literature under different terminology.
The transfer CDF is known and not a novelty component by itself.
Some related publisher-only full texts were not independently inspected; their claims were not represented as NOT_COVERING.

value.rationale: Diagonal randomization of a nullspace is explicitly intended to improve small-eigenvalue separation while controlling the original-system residual. Characterizing precisely when these two metrics must move in fixed proportion for every perturbation is a natural sharp structural boundary, not an arbitrary coordinate example; balanced symmetry is uniquely forced from all three coordinate probes. The sharp coefficient and joint acceptance probability make the distinction operational for this benchmark, while the limited dimension and infinitesimal regime are explicit.
